answer: Ask what a clone farm cannot buy in bulk, and the answer points at Proof of unique work visa with employer history. It requires a visa tied to employers over four years, so the wander of scaling up is a queue of real-world chores. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own a visa tied to employers over four years, and the ember grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The tundra is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
